steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Voting in elections is the most basic form of democratic participation, but citizens have many other routes to influence decisions. | Key Fact: Petitions to Parliament: if a petition on the UK Parliament website reaches 100,000 signatures, it must be considered for debate in Parliament. Petitions are a direct way for citizens to raise issues. | Key Fact: Pressure groups are organisations that aim to influence government policy without seeking election. Insider groups (e.g. BMA, CBI) have regular access to government. Outsider groups (e.g. Greenpeace, Extinction Rebellion) use public campaigns and direct action. | Key Fact: Lobbying involves directly contacting MPs, peers, or ministers to influence legislation or policy.
